storyboard.ears: 9% of young adults live with a partner — not a spouse.
Among the youngest adults, 9% live with a partner they never married. That's more than the number living with a spouse.
storyboard.evidence: U.S. Census Bureau (American Community Survey, reported by Bloomberg) | 18-24 year olds: living with an unmarried partner vs a spouse (percent) | https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-11-17/modern-love-cohabitation-on-rise-in-u-s-demographic-trends | 2026-11-05

storyboard.ears: In 1968, 82% of adults in their late twenties and early thirties lived with a spouse. Today, it's fewer than half.
storyboard.evidence: U.S. Census Bureau | 25-34 year olds living with a spouse, 1968 vs 2018 (percent) | https://www.census.gov/topics/families/families-and-households.html | 2026-11-05

storyboard.ears: Even older adults are doing it. Unmarried couples living together more than tripled since 2000, to 4.2 million.
storyboard.evidence: Bowling Green State University, National Center for Family & Marriage Research (using Census/ACS data) | Cohabiting adults aged 50+, 2000 vs 2022 (count) | https://www.bgsu.edu/ncfmr/resources/data/family-profiles/FP-24-14.html | 2026-11-05

storyboard.ears: If living together already beats marriage for the young, what happens to marriage next?
